title: Playing weddings, free food and fights; Kittman's band for the Bulls
summary: Weddings meant free food, drink and fights, with shorter hours. Rene says he played for the Bulls in Kittman's band.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yeah, that was, whoo, they'd go from Carlton to the barracks. That was the walkingest people I ever seen. They shouldn't walk. But now, one of the kickest things, boy, is that wedding business, about playing for wedding, everything was free. You know they had more fights at a wedding than they had at any dance. And you used to have to be at the Italian home, there was no one for fights. And all that fellas fight for free beer, free wine, free sandwich, cake, ice cream, and everything. And the fellas just all called for it, and they just stayed there and gobbled it up and after they get high and they fight. We used to get off early when they had weddings. Sometimes we had to play from, you know, from eight to two, and then sometimes eight to twelve. Eight to twelve, sometimes we'd knock off eleven o'clock, sometimes twelve thirty when they'd start to go to two o'clock. All that bad riding, everything is free, you see they get full. And then time your people put on the wedding, I'll tell you, they'd give you plenty to eat, and make a dish of salad there. I was a big eater then, partner. I used to go to town that time. Well.
Who did you play for when you, what band was it when you say you played for the Bulls?
